text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Frederick Chiluba directs the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) to declare war against tax evaders.
- A strike by Copperbelt University workers in the northern mining town of Kitwe enters its second day.
- Government predicts a critical food shortage and appeals to the World Food Programme for help.

- Former foreign affairs minister Vernon Mwaanga appeals to the supreme court against a high court ruling that he pays 10,000 pounds sterling as deposit in a case in which he has sued Newsweek International for libel.
- The Zambian Conferedation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry says the government must curb rampant corruption in the public service.
- Ten people are arrested in a joint operation by Zambia's Drug Enforcement Commission and Zimbabwe's Drug Squad for being in possession of 630 kilograms of dagga (marijuana).
